{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that exposure to handicap-related upward counterfactual thoughts following failure would reduce subsequent task effort and performance compared to control thoughts.",
  "design": "between-subjects with 2 conditions (handicap-related upward counterfactual condition vs. control condition)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "exposure to either handicap-related upward counterfactual thoughts or control thoughts after receiving failure feedback on an initial math test",
  "outcome_measure": "subsequent task effort and performance (number of items attempted and percent correct on a second math test)",
  "population_and_setting": "University of Konstanz students in a laboratory setting",
  "sample_size_total": 28,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "recruited in return for €5 or course credit",
  "analysis_plan": "one-tailed t-tests comparing conditions on stress reporting, items attempted, number correct, and percent correct",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants completed a prescreening measure including the Rosenberg Self-Esteem scale, completed an initial 2-min practice session and math exam, received failure feedback, read assigned statements, completed a stress inventory as an assessment of self-handicapping, and then completed a second math exam."
